metric: Distinct (query, rewrite) pairs, from 4,160 rewrites by 13 systems of TPC-H, DSB, Calcite and SQLStorm queries, that the authors' PostgreSQL run flagged equal, proved equivalent as result bags; 66 more are refuted by a replayed database (instance-label disagreements, left out of the denominator).
correctness: 0 wrong: every proof is replayed on the prover's counterexample, KumoSQL's targeted databases and, for TPC-H, a generated scale-0.01 instance; a difference counts only when DuckDB agrees with its optimizer off and, for order-sensitive queries, in three row orders
held_out: 349/555 proved, 0 wrong (a fifth of the queries, by hash, with all their rewrites)
caveats: Data downloaded at a pinned commit (no licence; not bundled). Flags come from one PostgreSQL instance, so a refuted pair is a label disagreement, not an error. Quoted upper-case identifiers are folded to lower case (the Calcite queries quote tables created in lower case) and FETCH FIRST n ROWS ONLY is read as LIMIT n. 2 pairs flagged both ways are not scored. Until 2026-11-10 no prover rule had been written for this eval; the baseline on that day, before the rules (main c384968, this harness): 1354/2608 proved, 0 wrong, held out 279/555. Eight rule modules were then written against the unknown development pairs (tailed_grouping_sets.py, tailed_outer_aggregates.py, wrapped_join_filters.py, closed_sources.py, listed_output_names.py, one_row_tails.py, string_spelling_rules.py, printed_spelling.py) with an interval-arithmetic reading in string_number_compare.py, so the development pairs are tuned on. The held-out fifth was not: its pairs were run for scoring only and never read one by one, and no proof was lost on either part. Earlier harness history: FETCH FIRST read as LIMIT (the 100 development pairs that use it, 81 flagged equal, went from 16/67 to 7/67 proved, 0 wrong, at the time) and a 30 s limit on replaying a TPC-H instance without the optimizer, both from development pairs.
